title: Canonical integral finite-extension maps and their conclusion predicates
statement: For a prime l, finite coefficient extensions E⊂L and a separated finite-type D.k-scheme X with l≠D.p, use the specified tensor, completion and finite dualizing models [def-sf-integral-finite-extension-models] and coherent dualizing data [def-sf-coherent-integral-dualizing-datum]. The unique map u is characterized by its finite counit reduction equations; beta is v followed by internal Hom into u. The identity unit and composition comp are the specified ordinary scalar unit/associator conjugated by completion. extendedEvaluation is scalar extension of evaluation with all completion comparisons. Conclusion, IdentityConclusion and CompositionConclusion are exactly the existing predicates of the integral finite-extension lemma. This relocates their existing signatures and bodies unchanged; u_reduction records the defining reduction equation as a proved theorem. No second construction or choice is introduced.

proof.text: Construct the compatible finite family by quotient.hom, extension of wE.reduction, finiteU and wL.reduction.inv. Apply integralConstructibleReductionHom to T omega_E and omega_L, using constructibility preservation and finiteDualizing_reduction_coherent. Cancel wL.reduction.hom to obtain existence and uniqueness. All code is relocated unchanged.

Define u by this unique characterization. Keep beta, unit, comp, extendedEvaluation and the three conclusion predicates verbatim. Extract u_reduction from the chosen witness specification; no new hole is introduced.
